checks.name: the-command
checks.summary: A4. Service.StartFraming is added in a NEW file internal/application/framing.go; no existing file in internal/application was edited except two closed-set guard test files (see the closed-set-guards-widened check). Measured shape: callerActor(ctx, RoleOwner, RoleScheduler), exactly Capture's pair, so a runner caller is refused; requireRequest(req.RequestID) and requestFingerprint("start-framing", req); s.mutate(ctx, "start-framing:"+req.RequestID, ...) with u.Idempotency(ctx, req.RequestID, "start-framing"), refusing a same-key different-fingerprint request with ErrIdempotencyConflict and replaying the prior response with restoreResponse; ErrNotFound for an absent Requirement; the ControlTarget's RepositoryID resolved from u.RequirementRepositoryLink inside the same transaction, empty when unlinked, following Plan; domain.Permit with Kind domain.PermitClaim against the revision derived from domain.EffectiveControl inside the transaction exactly as Capture derives it; domain.DecideRequirement with Kind domain.RequirementStartFraming, the caller's actor, the transaction authority time from transactionAuthorityTime (the same accessor Service.record uses) and ExpectedVersion from the request; u.SaveRequirement(ctx, next, r.Version); and s.record with operation "start-framing", aggregate type "requirement", event type "requirement.framing-started" and a NIL outbox argument. StartFramingRequest is {RequestID, RequirementID string; ExpectedVersion domain.Version} and carries no control_revision, no repository_id and no timestamp; StartFramingResponse is {RequirementID string; Status domain.RequirementStatus; Version domain.Version}. Nothing is passed to domain.EffectFromPermit. VERDICT: PASS. Measured: status captured -> framing, version 1 -> 2, exactly one event recorded with type requirement.framing-started on aggregate type requirement at the new version, ZERO outbox items staged, one idempotency record written, a replay of the same request_id returning the byte-identical prior response with no second event and no second transition, and a same-key different-fingerprint request refused with ErrIdempotencyConflict leaving the Requirement unchanged. The mechanical scan also measured 14 non-test files in the package and exactly ONE naming domain.RequirementStartFraming, in framing.go, which is C4 asserted rather than promised.

checks.name: seven-control-mode-table
checks.summary: A5. Table test over all seven control modes, one fresh Service and store per mode, driven through the real application Service over a real store, never through a hand-built domain.PermitDecision. MEASURED CELLS, verbatim from the run: allow -> start-framing ALLOWED (err=<nil>); pause-intake -> ALLOWED (err=<nil>); pause-claim -> DENIED (err=control policy denies operation); graceful-stop -> DENIED (control policy denies operation); immediate-stop -> DENIED (control policy denies operation); emergency-stop -> DENIED (control policy denies operation); cancel -> DENIED (control policy denies operation). 2 of 7 modes allow framing. Every cell matches A5's declared table exactly, and each is cross-checked against the package's existing permitAllowedTable mirror of domain.Permit's own per-kind gate; no cell contradicted, so no escalation. Every DENIED cell was asserted to leave the Requirement's status AND version AND the event count byte-unchanged, and to be attributable to domain.ErrControlDenied; every cell was asserted to change the outbox by zero items. THE TWO BOUNDARIES, asserted IN THE SAME RUN per mode: (1) under pause-intake at control revision 1, start-framing on an already-captured Requirement is ALLOWED while a FRESH Capture at that very same revision is DENIED with `control policy denies operation` -- that asymmetry is the whole reason the kind is claim and not intake, and it is what "take no new work in, finish what you already have" means; the measured fresh-capture row for the same seven modes is allow ALLOWED, pause-intake DENIED, pause-claim ALLOWED, graceful-stop DENIED, immediate-stop DENIED, emergency-stop DENIED, cancel DENIED. (2) under emergency-stop, framing is DENIED, which is the property a permit-free command would not have. The design's load-bearing point is confirmed structurally too: because the command stages no durable effect, nothing is passed to domain.EffectFromPermit, whose Allow-only test would otherwise have denied framing under pause-intake.
